rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 5 µA constant DC, implanted subcutaneous stimulator, 2 wk, contralateral dummy electrodes | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: ⭐ IDENTICAL cyclic load, TWO different bones, OPPOSITE length results
rows.direction: ⭐ Fetal rat METATARSAL: loaded bones grew LESS than controls (p<0.05). Fetal rat FEMUR: same regimen, loaded bones grew SIGNIFICANTLY MORE (p<0.001). The clearest evidence in the domain that the sign of the mechanical response is BONE-SPECIFIC, not universal
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 0.4 N at 0.77 Hz, 30 s bouts, ex vivo culture, portable loading device | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: ⭐ VIBRATION — the ONLY registered HUMAN trial with a BONE-LENGTH primary outcome
rows.direction: UNKNOWN — trial status UNKNOWN, n=40 planned, NO RESULTS POSTED
rows.source: HUMAN, children 6–12 y with leg-length discrepancy. NCT03666975, University College London
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: LivMD platform, 30 Hz, 0.4 g vs 1.0 g, 15 min, 3×/wk × 10 wk; shorter leg on the plate, longer leg on a static block; 4 mo pre / 3 mo treat / 6 mo post; laser+ultrasound leg length monthly | HUMAN DATA?: YES (registered, unreported)

rows.direction: Bone formation orientation, chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs, OA cartilage repair. No growth-plate or length endpoint in any species found
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 180 mT to 1–2 T | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: CHIROPRACTIC "vibration traction" / spinal decompression for DISC HEIGHT
rows.direction: Radiographic disc-height increase claimed; uncontrolled case series
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: multimodal rehabilitation + vibration traction, retrospective case series | HUMAN DATA?: Yes (very weak)

rows.concept: ⭐ PERIOSTEAL RESECTION measured in REAL TIME with microtransducers
rows.direction: ⭐ Growth velocity increased in EVERY lamb at EVERY timepoint, immediately and sustained. Mechanism identified: AXIAL ELONGATION OF THE HYPERTROPHIC CHONDROCYTE, not proliferation, not swelling magnitude, not matrix. Authors propose it as an adjunct to counteract the growth INHIBITION of distraction osteogenesis
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: proximal tibial periosteal resection, 5 lambs, 10 µm resolution, up to 7 wk | HUMAN DATA?: See rows 20–21

rows.concept: CHONDRODIATASIS (slow symmetric distraction THROUGH an open physis)
aliases: slow symmetric distraction THROUGH an open physis
rows.direction: Length gains up to 36% (LLD) and 64.5% (achondroplasia) of segment length, 170 segments in 75 children. ⛔ Mechanism is NOT stimulation of the plate — thymidine labelling, sulfate labelling and microcirculation all UNCHANGED in rabbit. ⛔ Premature physeal closure with LOSS of gained length in 5/5 femora <13 y
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: ~0.25 mm ×4/day or less, dynamic axial fixator, physis still open | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: LOADING FREQUENCY for cortical bone formation (adult)
rows.direction: Frequency modulates bone-formation rate. Establishes the frequency-response shape in the bone (not cartilage) compartment
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 1–10 Hz at matched strain, rat ulna | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.direction: ⭐ POSITIVE: tibia ~+1%, femur ~+1.4% after ONE WEEK (both P<0.001); tibial elongation RATE +6%. Up to +1.5% in the 2-week protocol. Functional: loaded-side weight bearing +20%
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 40 °C, 40 min/day, one side; contralateral side ~30 °C; 1–2 wk; weanling mice | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: Ilizarov DISTRACTION RATE and RHYTHM (the classic parameter study)
rows.direction: Osteogenesis quality depends on BOTH rate and frequency; higher subdivision of the same daily rate is better. Companion paper: fixation stability and periosteal/medullary preservation matter
rows.source: dog tibia PMID 2912628 (Part II) and PMID 2910611 (Part I); clinical PMID 2403497
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: rates 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 mm per day × frequencies 1, 4 or 60 steps per day; open osteotomy vs closed osteoclasis | HUMAN DATA?: Clinical

rows.concept: Diurnal stature loss in CHILDREN + the "stretched" measurement technique
rows.direction: Loss 0.31 cm (0900→1100) and 0.20 cm (1100→1300), no further loss after ~6 h up. Stretching did NOT reduce diurnal loss but added 0.28 cm to the recorded height. Afternoon appointments recommended
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: measured 0900/1100/1300/1500, stretched vs unstretched | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: Guided growth of the PROXIMAL FEMUR
rows.direction: Extends growth modulation beyond the knee
rows.source: lamb PMID 20864854; construct comparison PMID 22327457; fatigue failure PMID 26523701
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: screw/plate constructs, lamb pilot | HUMAN DATA?: YES (clinical technique)

rows.concept: ⭐ VERTEBRAL BODY TETHERING (anterior spinal growth modulation)
rows.direction: Measured DIFFERENTIAL SEGMENTAL GROWTH of vertebrae in vivo — 51 patients, 764 vertebrae; concave-side vertebral growth magnitude is the primary determinant of response; maintained at 4 years across 888 peri-apical vertebrae
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: flexible tether under tension across the convexity | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: DYNAMIC/cyclic compression at an elevated MEAN stress
rows.direction: Growth rate REDUCED vs sham at both usable settings, with growth-plate height, hypertrophic cell height and proliferative count all UNCHANGED. Combined high magnitude + high frequency destroyed the tissue (inflammation)
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: mean 0.2 MPa, ±0.06 MPa at 1.0 Hz; ±0.2 MPa at 0.1 Hz; ±0.14 MPa at 1.0 Hz; 15 d implanted device | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: Compressive repetitive loading through a SMALL joint (gymnast wrist)
rows.direction: Distal radial physeal injury with acquired POSITIVE ULNAR VARIANCE — an internally controlled human demonstration that repetitive compression through a small joint arrests a physis
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: weight-bearing on the upper limb during growth | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.direction: ⭐ HUMAN LENGTH GAIN WITHOUT ANY DRUG: mean femoral overgrowth 10.5 ± 7.3 mm after internal fixation (ESIN 9.9 vs MIPO 11.2 mm, ns); greater in length-UNSTABLE fractures (12.3 vs 9.2 mm, p=0.048). Separately, overgrowth avg 1.17 cm in the first 18 months in 77.4% of children; greater with proximal-third fractures and age <8 y
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: diaphyseal fracture in a growing child | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: LOADING FREQUENCY on isolated growth-plate chondrocytes (in vitro)
rows.direction: DNA synthesis up at 30 and 150 cycles/min (0.5 and 2.5 Hz); collagen and proteoglycan synthesis rose WITH frequency. A dose-response in the frequency dimension that has never been taken in vivo
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: intermittent TENSILE stress at varied frequency; rib growth-plate chondrocytes, proliferating (d4) and matrix-forming (d11) | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: ⭐ EMBRYO MOVEMENT as a determinant of LIMB PROPORTIONS
rows.direction: Altered movement changes limb PROPORTIONS and regulates chondrocyte proliferation in ONLY SPECIFIC growth plates — selectivity determined by intrinsic mTOR pathway activity in each individual plate. A mechanism for why the same load gives opposite answers in different bones (row 109)
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: incubation temperature → motility; pharmacological immobilisation of chick embryos | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: GROWING RODS / magnetically controlled growing rods (axial distraction of the spine)
rows.direction: Frequency of lengthening affects the height achieved (dual growing rod series). Direct human axial distraction with a length endpoint (T1–S1)
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: repeated lengthenings; frequency varied | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: ⭐ VOLUNTARY WHEEL RUNNING (chronic, high-volume) as a SOLUTE-DELIVERY intervention
rows.direction: ⭐ POSITIVE: ALL runners had significantly longer limbs regardless of temperature. TAIL length responded only to temperature — the internal control proving the effect is LOCAL to loaded limb bones, not systemic endocrine. Multiphoton imaging showed enhanced solute delivery to the tibial growth plate measured AT REST under anaesthesia = a lasting vascular adaptation
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 11 days free wheel access, 16 °C or 25 °C housing | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: ⭐ SURGICALLY INDUCED ARTERIOVENOUS FISTULA to lengthen a limb
rows.direction: Four human papers 1961–1974 on the effect on leg length, incl. 10-year observations — direction and magnitude UNVERIFIED (no abstracts in PubMed for any of them)
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: AV fistula created in the shorter leg | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: PULSED ELECTROMAGNETIC FIELD (PEMF) during limb lengthening — HUMAN, double-blind
rows.direction: NO effect on the rate or amount of regenerate bone. DID prevent disuse bone LOSS distal to the gap (BMD −10% vs −33% at 2 mo). No length endpoint
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: active vs inactive coil, 13 patients (mean age ~12–13 y), Villarubbias lengthening | HUMAN DATA?: YES (regenerate, not stature)

rows.concept: THERAPEUTIC ULTRASOUND applied over an open physis
rows.direction: HIGH dose = pathological: epiphyseal flattening, tibial plateau wedging, disordered proliferative zone, lateral physis height 1084 µm vs 500 (therapeutic) vs 531 (contralateral). Therapeutic dose no adverse effect short-term
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 0.5 W/cm² (therapeutic) vs 2.2 W/cm² (~45× dose), 20 min/day × 6 wk, over the knee | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: THERAPEUTIC ULTRASOUND — systematic review of physeal effects
rows.direction: High dose → necrosis + growth inhibition; LOW dose → transient STIMULATORY effect on growth, thicker hypertrophic zone, thicker whole plate. No human growth disturbance reported; review recommends avoiding the physis
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 8 animal studies | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: SUSTAINED TENSILE DISTRACTION of vertebrae + disc (growing-rod analogue)
rows.direction: In vivo mechanobiology of vertebral and disc growth under sustained tension
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: sustained tension, mouse tail model | HUMAN DATA?: Analogue of human growing rods

rows.concept: PERIOSTEAL STRIPPING + DIVISION (PSPD) — HUMAN, modern controlled series
rows.direction: ΔLLD −13.9 mm vs −3.2 mm in controls (significant). Age was the significant predictor; cut-off 9.6 years — >10 mm correction unlikely above ~10 y of age
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: PSPD at implant removal; 10 treated vs 6 declining controls; mean follow-up 4.3 y | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: PERIOSTEAL DIVISION combined with compression or distraction
rows.direction: Periosteal division enhanced growth at the ADJACENT plate and INHIBITED it distally; it amplified distraction and blunted compression. Authors conclude the mechanism is at least partly MECHANICAL (release of a periosteal tether)
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 1 kg compression or distraction ± circumferential periosteal division + 1 cm strip, 6 wk | HUMAN DATA?: —

rows.direction: PROXIMAL (adjacent to the target physis) division was the most effective of the three
rows.source: rat tibia PMID 3680349; chondrocyte kinetics PMID 3654353
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: proximal release vs distal release vs full diaphyseal strip | HUMAN DATA?: —

rows.concept: DUTY CYCLE of sustained compression (24 h vs 12 h)
rows.direction: Full-time loading suppressed growth MORE than intermittent: vertebra 82% (full) vs 93% (day) vs 90% (night) of control; tibia 70% vs 84% vs 86%
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 0.1 MPa, 24/24 h vs 12/24 h day vs 12/24 h night, 8 d | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.direction: Hemicircumferential incision → 1–2 mm overgrowth plus 5–10° valgus and an S-shaped deformity; direction of the cut determines the deformity → supports the mechanical (not humoral) theory
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: longitudinal vs hemicircumferential incision | HUMAN DATA?: —

rows.direction: NO peer-reviewed height endpoint exists. The indexed literature is renal-calculus clearance, lumbar disc symptoms, EMG relaxation and cervical cord injury from falls. Commercial height claims rest on transient disc rehydration (row 41)
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 30–60° tilt, minutes | HUMAN DATA?: Yes (not for height)

rows.concept: LOW-LEVEL LASER THERAPY over the femoral physis
rows.direction: NEGATIVE: percentage femoral longitudinal length LOWER in the irradiated group at day 21. Calcified cartilage zone and angiogenesis increased (i.e. accelerated closure direction)
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: GaAlAs 830 nm, 40 mW, 10 J/cm², one point, daily up to 21 d | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: LOW-LEVEL LASER THERAPY, 670 nm, dose series
rows.direction: NULL on limb length and on all plate histology at every dose
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 4, 8 and 16 J/cm², right tibia, contralateral control, followed to 14 wk | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.direction: Rest insertion combined with high-frequency loading ENHANCES osteogenesis; cortical response saturates quickly without it. Bone-formation endpoints only — never tested on a growth plate
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 10-s rest inserted between cycles; and loading duration × rest insertion factorial | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: Sustained DISTRACTION (tension) across a growth plate
rows.direction: POSITIVE and on the same line as compression — distraction accelerates growth; sensitivity is the mirror of row 1
rows.source: rat/rabbit/calf PMID 16705695; rabbit 1 kg distraction PMID 2312573
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: same rig, tensile stress up to ~0.1 MPa | HUMAN DATA?: No direct normal-child data

rows.concept: FOOT PROGRESSION ANGLE / gait modification as a non-invasive growth-plate load lever
rows.direction: Changes hip contact forces and femoral growth-plate mechanics in children — a zero-cost, zero-device way to change physeal loading. Modelling only, no growth endpoint
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: altered foot progression angle, musculoskeletal + FE modelling | HUMAN DATA?: Modelling

rows.concept: Loading FREQUENCY for the lateral-joint modality
rows.direction: Frequency-dependent bone FORMATION (proxy, not length). Establishes the effective band is 5–20 Hz
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 0.5 N at 5, 10, 15 Hz, 3 min/day | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.direction: ⭐⭐ POSITIVE AND THE LARGEST IN THE DOMAIN. Femur +2.3% vs contralateral / +3.5% vs age-matched; tibia +2.3% / +3.7%; all P<0.001. Proximal tibial plate height +19.5%, plate cross-sectional area +30.7%; hypertrophic zone chondrocyte NUMBER and CELL HEIGHT both up
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 0.5 N, 5-min bouts/day, piezoelectric loader across the knee, contralateral control | HUMAN DATA?: NO — never tested in a human

rows.concept: MICROWAVE THERMAL ABLATION of the physis (minimally invasive epiphysiodesis)
rows.direction: Thermal destruction of the plate to ARREST growth — the deliberate opposite direction, and proof that a percutaneous thermal device can reach and change a physis
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 65 W, 90–270 s, antenna adjacent to the proximal tibial plate | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: Sustained axial COMPRESSION across a growth plate (Hueter–Volkmann)
rows.direction: NEGATIVE, linear, no dead band. Growth-rate sensitivity 17.1%/0.1 MPa (range 9.2–23.9); vertebra 15.0 vs proximal tibia 18.6
rows.source: rat, rabbit, calf; caudal vertebra + proximal tibia; fluorochrome interlabel length PMID 16705695
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: ~0.1–0.2 MPa, external fixator, 8 d, continuous | HUMAN DATA?: Inferred only (scoliosis, Blount, brace)

rows.direction: Warm-reared limbs permanently LONGER; effect is on the extremities (Allen's rule), acts by directly modulating cartilage growth, not only by selection
rows.source: mouse PMID 19047632; review/index PMID 24715562; window PMID 23956063
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: chronic housing at ~16 °C vs 25 °C from weaning | HUMAN DATA?: No (ecological correlation only)

rows.concept: ⭐ LATERAL joint loading at the ELBOW (forelimb replication)
rows.direction: POSITIVE: humerus +1.2%; ulna +1.7% vs contralateral, +3.4% vs age-matched. c-fos/egr1/atf3 rose not only at the elbow but at the wrist and shoulder of the loaded limb
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 0.5 N class dynamic load, 5-min bouts/day × 10 d | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.direction: POSITIVE BUT TRANSIENT: femur only 1.5% longer at 4 weeks (P<0.001), NOT maintained; diaphyseal diameter progressively NARROWER at every timepoint
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: full diaphyseal strip, single operation | HUMAN DATA?: see rows 18–19

rows.concept: PERIOSTEAL RESECTION combined with guided growth
rows.direction: Adding periosteal resection made the guided-growth construct significantly more efficient (2.5°/mm faster deformation) — i.e. the two mechanical levers, growth retardation and growth acceleration, are ADDITIVE
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: modular plate ± periosteal resection, 16 lambs | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: HINDLIMB UNLOADING (tail suspension) — the ground analogue
rows.direction: Longitudinal growth rate largely unaffected (row 37); tail-suspended controls did not differ from other controls on plate histomorphometry. Bone MASS falls
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 5–21 d suspension | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: PERIOSTEAL STRIPPING — HUMAN, post-polio limb shortening
rows.direction: Relative length increase in the majority, but the response was haphazard and unpredictable; recommended only for minor discrepancy
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: long lower-limb bones, 30 children, 5-year follow-up | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.direction: Physiological HP is chondroprotective/chondroinductive; injurious HP is degradative. HP prevents chondrocyte differentiation via heterochromatin remodelling — i.e. it holds cells in the chondrocyte state
rows.source: mouse growth-plate + articular explants PMID 38144567; PMID 33310912; human chondrocytes PMID 12507587
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: physiological vs injurious HP, ex vivo explants, RNA-seq; and 1–10 MPa 1 Hz in chondrocytes | HUMAN DATA?: No length endpoint

rows.concept: Vertebral vs DISC contribution to spinal height growth
rows.direction: Vertebral height growth PREDOMINATES over intervertebral disc height growth in adolescents — bounds how much of trunk height any disc-directed mechanical intervention can reach
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: stereoradiographs, ages 7.5–20 y | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: TEMPERATURE and bone growth in the CHICK (early comparative work)
rows.direction: Companion to the Serrat/Allen's-rule line; no abstract, UNVERIFIED
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: — | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: ⭐ RADIAL EXTRACORPOREAL SHOCKWAVE (rESWT) directly on the growth plate
rows.direction: ⭐ POSITIVE LENGTH ENDPOINT: high-dose bone length 4.46 ± 0.75 mm vs control 3.50 ± 0.38 mm, p=0.01; proliferative chondrocyte number up. Explicitly avascular/ex vivo, so the effect is LOCAL and not systemic-GF-dependent
rows.source: fetal rat metatarsal organ culture (Sävendahl lab) PMID 31794485; commentary PMID 32011380
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: single application; low 500 imp/5 Hz/90 mJ, mid 500/5 Hz/120 mJ, high 500 imp/10 Hz/180 mJ; 14 d culture | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: PREOPERATIVE COTREL DYNAMIC TRACTION for scoliosis
rows.direction: Historical randomised pilot and several series; correction endpoints only. No stature endpoint
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: longitudinal traction ± exercises ± casting | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: DISTRACTION EPIPHYSIOLYSIS (rapid physeal separation, distinct from chondrodiatasis)
rows.direction: A lengthening method with defined experimental, morphological and clinical series; forces monitored continuously
rows.source: rabbit + HUMAN, PMID 7471563 (I, experimental), 7009012 (II, morphology), 7471565 (III, clinical), 1561874, 3392584
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: high-rate distraction that fractures through the hypertrophic zone | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: DIURNAL stature variation (disc creep and rehydration)
rows.direction: Mean circadian variation 19.3 mm = 1.1% of stature; 54% of the loss in the FIRST HOUR after rising; ~70% regained in the first half of the night. Shrinkage rises NON-linearly with load; repetitive lifting shrinks more than the equivalent static load; Fowler's position recovers faster than standing
rows.source: HUMAN, n=8 adults, PMID 4002039; ankylosing spondylitis PMID 23915708; heel-pad artefact PMID 15676749
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 24 h cycle; static shoulder loads 2.5–40 kg; repetitive lifting | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: LIPUS on the MANDIBULAR CONDYLE (a secondary growth cartilage)
rows.direction: 20 min > 10 min; stimulates chondrogenesis AND osteogenesis and enhances endochondral bone formation; gross condylar dimension change non-significant. A dose-response exists for LIPUS on a growth cartilage
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 20 min/day × 20 or 28 days, unilateral or bilateral | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: PIEZO1 / primary cilium as the transducer of compressive stress at the physis
rows.direction: PIEZO1–primary cilium axis mediates compressive-stress-induced growth-plate degeneration and ossification; PIEZO1–GPX4/ferroptosis in vertebral plate dysplasia
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: compressive loading, AIS models | HUMAN DATA?: Human tissue

rows.concept: SLEEP DEPRIVATION and the stature rhythm
rows.direction: Decreased stature and blunted the 24-h rhythm in young and middle-aged men; regained on the first recovery night. The rhythm is driven by RECUMBENCY, not an endogenous clock
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: one night of deprivation | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: Non-invasive AC electrical stimulation of the epiphyseal plate — PATENT
rows.direction: Claimed physeal stimulation. PATENT, not a study — no data
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 2.5–15 V p-p at 20–100 kHz, surface electrodes | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: ⭐ HIGH-IMPACT JUMPING in short-stature children (controlled trial)
rows.direction: ⭐ HEIGHT GAIN 4.200 cm vs 2.478 cm in controls, p=0.001; femoral-neck BMD Z +1.075. ⚠ Mediation analysis internally incoherent (indirect effect via BMD NEGATIVE, β=−0.442, no direct effect)
rows.source: HUMAN, 47 prepubertal children 8–11 y, PMID 41233903 (non-randomised; ChiCTR2500095544)
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 3 sessions/wk, 50 min/session, 24 weeks, progressive jumping | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: Trans-physeal mineralised BRIDGES as mechanical "base isolation"
rows.direction: Proposes that physeal bridges exist to minimise epiphyseal SHEAR — a structural constraint on how much shear a plate can be given
rows.source: preprint/record, PMID NA (2026 EPMC record, no PMID) — UNVERIFIED
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: native anatomy | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: ⭐⭐ RECUMBENCY as the permissive state for elongation (implanted microtransducers)
rows.direction: ⭐ AT LEAST 90% OF BONE ELONGATION OCCURS DURING RECUMBENCY AND ALMOST NONE DURING STANDING OR LOCOMOTION. The single most decision-relevant mechanical fact in the domain: growth is mechanically GATED by unloading, in real time
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: continuous sampling every 167 s for 21–25 days, immature lambs, free-ranging | HUMAN DATA?: No (hypothesised for children; the "growing pains" link)

rows.direction: Enhances callus consolidation (regenerate endpoint). Combined with BMP-2 in rats
rows.source: HUMAN tibia lengthening-over-nail (PMC6419405, PMID UNVERIFIED); rat PMID 35594008
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: standard LIPUS protocol during/after distraction | HUMAN DATA?: Yes (regenerate)

rows.direction: HSP70-mediated; the combined stimulus is more chondroinductive than either alone. Links the mechanical and thermal arms (rows 12–15) at the cell level
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: HP with a transient temperature rise 32.5→38.7 °C | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: SPACEFLIGHT / true microgravity — animal longitudinal growth rate
rows.direction: Skeletal unloading generally did NOT change longitudinal growth rate, regardless of age, strain, sex, duration or method — one exception, −34% in slow-growing ovariectomised rats hindlimb-elevated 8 d. Col2 mRNA −33%, aggrecan −53% after 11-d flight
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 4–14 day flights (PSE 1/3/4, PARE 3, COSMOS 2044) | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: EXPERIMENTAL VENOUS LIGATION (venous stasis) and bone growth
rows.direction: Bone growth and blood flow measured together — direction UNVERIFIED, no abstract
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: ligation of limb veins | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: JUMPING in normal children — bone endpoints only
rows.direction: Hip and spine BMC gains; height used as a COVARIATE. No analysed height endpoint
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 100 jumps/day 3×/wk (Fuchs) ; 25 jumps/day from 45 cm box 5 d/wk × 12 wk (Gunter) | HUMAN DATA?: YES (height measured, unanalysed)

rows.direction: Rebound growth is common and its risk factors are age, correction rate and residual growth; rabbit model quantifies incidence and chronology
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: implant removal after correction | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: Vertebral WEDGING: growth vs remodelling partition
rows.direction: Wedging is partly asymmetric growth (Hueter–Volkmann) and partly diaphyseal remodelling (Wolff) — the two mechanical laws act simultaneously
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: imposed 30° angulation + 0.1 or 0.2 MPa, three ages of rat | HUMAN DATA?: Human modelling PMID 17653775

rows.concept: BIPEDAL walking / standing imposed on a quadruped (loading history)
rows.direction: Percentage change in tibia and femur length differed for fully-loaded bipedal walking and bipedal standing; NO absolute length differences — authors conclude loading moderates growth VELOCITY not final length
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: treadmill-harness, 12 wk, 5 conditions: fully-loaded biped walk, partially loaded, standing, quadrupedal, control | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.concept: ⭐ HALO-GRAVITY TRACTION (sustained axial spinal traction in children)
aliases: sustained axial spinal traction in children
rows.direction: Substantial radiographic correction of severe deformity and improved pulmonary function. Height/T1–S1 gain is real but is deformity correction, not physeal growth
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: halo + progressive weights, weeks to months, preoperative | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: Computational / FE models of physeal growth modulation
aliases: FE models of physeal growth modulation
rows.direction: Predict proliferative/hypertrophic zone response and validate against the Stokes dose-response. Models, not experiments
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: sustained load models; tension-band plate FE; foot-progression FE | HUMAN DATA?: Modelling

rows.direction: Title says "Attempt to…" — no abstract in PubMed, direction UNVERIFIED
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: mechanical vibration to a growing dog limb | HUMAN DATA?: No

rows.direction: NO length effect reported. Cortical BMC and cortical area rose at 5 wk; "bone size" was measured but only cortical geometry reported. A bone-MASS result
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: 50 Hz, 0.5 g, 15 min/day, 5 d/wk, 5 or 10 wk, from 5 wk of age | HUMAN DATA?: see rows 24–25

rows.concept: ⭐ GYMNASTICS — the human natural experiment, and it splits by discipline
rows.direction: Elite male artistic gymnasts: final height SDS BELOW genetic target; final height correlated NEGATIVELY with training intensity (r=−0.252, p=0.022). Elite female ARTISTIC gymnasts also below target; elite female RHYTHMIC gymnasts EXCEEDED target height
rows.source: HUMAN, n=86 males PMID 22768655; n=215 RG + 113 AG PMID 22450345
rows.note: DOSE PARAMETERS: ≥ years of elite training from early childhood | HUMAN DATA?: YES

rows.concept: Bipedal/quadruped joint-load ontogeny and cam morphology
rows.direction: Growth plate reorients to minimise shear; altered hip loading predicts cam deformity — proof that habitual load direction shapes physeal ORIENTATION
